The elders with idols in the temple (Ezekiel 8)

precepts.text: When she saw men pourtrayed upon the wall, the images of the Chaldeans pourtrayed with vermilion, as soon as she saw them with her eyes, she doted upon them, and sent messengers unto them into Chaldea. That is why the Lord said in Numbers 15, when he gave us the fringes, that with your eyes ye go a whoring.
precepts.point: Seventy men of the ancients of the house of Israel stood with censers in the dark, saying, the Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth. What do you do in the dark? Your secret sins.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

precepts.why:
When Ezekiel dug in the wall, he saw “every form of creeping things, and abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, pourtrayed upon the wall round about.” That is like putting the images of Cesare Borgia on the walls, or Guadalupe on the walls, today. Ezekiel 23 shows what they were putting on the walls: images of the gods of their enemies.

“Then I saw that she was defiled, that they took both one way, And that she increased her whoredoms: for when she saw men pourtrayed upon the wall, the images of the Chaldeans pourtrayed with vermilion, Girded with girdles upon their loins, exceeding in dyed attire upon their heads, all of them princes to look to, after the manner of the Babylonians of Chaldea”. Israel looked at the pictures of her enemies on the wall, dressed up like princes.

“And as soon as she saw them with her eyes, she doted upon them, and sent messengers unto them into Chaldea.” As soon as she saw them, she wanted them. That is why the Lord said in Numbers 15, when he gave us the fringes, that with your eyes you will go a whoring.

So the imagery on the walls of the temple in Ezekiel 8 was not harmless decoration. The images of other nations and their gods drew Israel's eyes, and her eyes drew her heart after them. It is the same today with the images hung on our walls, and it is why the Lord said, I cannot be around you all, and went far off from his sanctuary.

precepts.text: The capital of Ephraim is Samaria, proving Aholah/Samaria is the northern kingdom of Ephraim.
precepts.point: The elder is Aholah and her sister is Aholibah; they were the Most High's and bare sons and daughters. Aholah is Samaria, the northern kingdom, and Aholibah is Jerusalem, the southern kingdom.

note.label: Ezekiel 23: Aholah and Aholibah, the Two Harlot Sisters

precepts.why:
“Samaria is Aholah, and Jerusalem Aholibah.” To know who Aholah is, you have to know whose city Samaria was. Isaiah says it: “the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son.”

The capital of Ephraim is Samaria. So Aholah the elder, Samaria, is the northern kingdom of Ephraim. The two women, the daughters of one mother, are an allegory to depict the whoredoms we committed as a nation, and Aholah is the northern half of it.

precepts.text: Judah, Benjamin, and Levi were the ones the Most High raised up to return and build the house in Jerusalem, marking the southern kingdom as Aholibah/Jerusalem.
precepts.point: The elder is Aholah and her sister is Aholibah; they were the Most High's and bare sons and daughters. Aholah is Samaria, the northern kingdom, and Aholibah is Jerusalem, the southern kingdom.

note.label: Ezekiel 23: Aholah and Aholibah, the Two Harlot Sisters

precepts.why:
Aholibah is Jerusalem. When the captivity returned, “Then rose up the chief of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests, and the Levites, with all them whose spirit God had raised, to go up to build the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem.”

Judah, Benjamin and Levi were the ones the Most High raised up to return and build the house in Jerusalem. Those tribes are the southern kingdom. So Aholibah, Jerusalem, is the southern kingdom, the sister of Aholah, Samaria, the northern kingdom. Both were the Most High's, both bare sons and daughters, and both committed whoredoms in their youth in Egypt, where their breasts were pressed and the teats of their virginity bruised; Israel was already living loose.

precepts.text: Ephraim made a covenant with the Assyrians while oil was carried into Egypt, which is how we thought to trust upon them.
precepts.point: She committed her whoredoms with the chosen men of Assyria and defiled herself with all their idols, and she never left the whoredoms she brought from Egypt, for in her youth they lay with her and bruised her breasts. The whoredom is idolatry taking place in the spirit realm.

note.label: Ezekiel 23: Aholah and Aholibah, the Two Harlot Sisters

precepts.why:
Aholah “doted on her lovers, on the Assyrians her neighbours”. To dote is to love to excess or extravagance; the northern kingdom was overdoing it, excessively in love upon the Assyrians clothed with blue, captains and rulers, desirable young men riding upon horses. Hosea shows what that doting looked like: “Ephraim feedeth on wind, and followeth after the east wind: he daily increaseth lies and desolation; and they do make a covenant with the Assyrians, and oil is carried into Egypt.”

Ephraim, the northern kingdom, made a covenant with the Assyrians while oil was carried into Egypt. That is how we thought to trust upon them, going to Assyria and to Egypt at the same time. She committed her whoredoms with the chosen men of Assyria and “with all their idols she defiled herself”, and “Neither left she her whoredoms brought from Egypt”.

The whoredom is idolatry taking place in the spirit realm. She played the harlot while she was still the Most High's, feeding on wind.

precepts.text: The Assyrian shall be their king because they refused to return, and the sword shall abide on their cities.
precepts.point: She became famous among women, for judgment was executed upon her, the way everybody knows when a woman has been run through. Everybody knew the northern kingdom was gone.

note.label: Ezekiel 23: Aholah and Aholibah, the Two Harlot Sisters

precepts.why:
Because she doted on them, “I have delivered her into the hand of her lovers, into the hand of the Assyrians”. Hosea says the same of Ephraim: “He shall not return into the land of Egypt, but the Assyrian shall be his king, because they refused to return.”

The lover she doted on became her master. The Assyrian shall be their king because they refused to return to the Most High, and the sword abides on their cities. So the Assyrians “discovered her nakedness: they took her sons and her daughters, and slew her with the sword”.

precepts.text: In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria and carried Israel away captive into Assyria, when the judgment came to pass.
precepts.point: She became famous among women, for judgment was executed upon her, the way everybody knows when a woman has been run through. Everybody knew the northern kingdom was gone.

note.label: Ezekiel 23: Aholah and Aholibah, the Two Harlot Sisters

precepts.why:
Here is when the judgment came to pass. “In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.”

Samaria is Aholah. Delivered into the hand of the Assyrians upon whom she doted, they took her sons and daughters and slew her with the sword. “and she became famous among women; for they had executed judgment upon her.” The way everybody knows when a woman has been run through, everybody knew the northern kingdom was gone.

precepts.text: The Most High addresses the seed of the adulterer and the whore who inflame themselves with idols under every green tree, who enlarged the bed, made a covenant with the heathen, and debased themselves even unto hell, stooping from the Most High down to idols made with hands.
precepts.point: As soon as she saw them with her eyes she doted upon them and sent messengers to them into Chaldea, going after them immediately.

note.label: Ezekiel 23: Aholah and Aholibah, the Two Harlot Sisters

precepts.why:
Judah saw “the images of the Chaldeans pourtrayed with vermilion”, princes to look upon after the manner of Babylon, and “as soon as she saw them with her eyes, she doted upon them”. She was enticed by the flashy artwork and gold, just as a harlot is enticed by a man flashing his wealth, and sent messengers to them into Chaldea immediately.

Isaiah speaks to that same seed: “draw near hither, ye sons of the sorceress, the seed of the adulterer and the whore.” They are “children of transgression, a seed of falsehood, Enflaming yourselves with idols under every green tree, slaying the children in the valleys”. Their portion is the smooth stones of the stream, to which they poured a drink offering. “Should I receive comfort in these?”

“Upon a lofty and high mountain hast thou set thy bed”. Behind the doors and the posts she set up her remembrance, “for thou hast discovered thyself to another than me, and art gone up; thou hast enlarged thy bed, and made thee a covenant with them; thou lovedst their bed where thou sawest it.” That is Judah: she enlarged the bed, made a covenant with the heathen, and debased herself even unto hell, stooping from the Most High down to idols made with hands. She loved their bed the moment she saw it.

precepts.text: The adulteress decks her bed with coverings and perfumes it with myrrh to entice her lover, the same way we prepared the bed of love for the Babylonians.
precepts.point: Yet she multiplied her whoredoms, calling to remembrance the days of her youth in Egypt, for she doted upon paramours whose flesh is as the flesh of asses and whose issue is like that of horses. Like a harlot who keeps seeking bigger because she has stopped feeling, we constantly sought the nations with the biggest and baddest idols.

note.label: Ezekiel 23: Aholah and Aholibah, the Two Harlot Sisters

precepts.why:
“And the Babylonians came to her into the bed of love”. The strange woman in Proverbs shows how that bed is prepared: “I have decked my bed with coverings of tapestry, with carved works, with fine linen of Egypt. I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon. Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning: let us solace ourselves with loves.”

That is the same way we prepared the bed of love for the Babylonians. And they “defiled her with their whoredom, and she was polluted with them, and her mind was alienated from them.” Just as a woman who lies with a man she is not married to becomes alienated and is left out there, so the Most High alienated His mind from us: “then my mind was alienated from her, like as my mind was alienated from her sister.”

Yet she multiplied her whoredoms, calling to remembrance the days of her youth in Egypt, doting upon paramours “whose flesh is as the flesh of asses, and whose issue is like the issue of horses.” Like a harlot who keeps seeking bigger because she has stopped feeling, we constantly sought the nations with the biggest and baddest idols.

precepts.text: It is forbidden to let any of thy seed pass through the fire to Molech or to profane the name of the Most High, the cult sacrifice they were committing.
precepts.point: They defiled His sanctuary the same day and profaned His sabbaths, for when they had slain their children to their idols they came the very same day into His sanctuary to profane it, one foot in and one foot out, exactly as we still do when we sin all night and sit in church the next morning.

note.label: Ezekiel 23: Aholah and Aholibah, the Two Harlot Sisters

precepts.why:
Among the abominations Ezekiel is to declare: they “caused their sons, whom they bare unto me, to pass for them through the fire, to devour them.” The law forbade exactly that: “thou shalt not let any of thy seed pass through the fire to Molech, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am the Lord.”

That is the cult sacrifice they were committing, and it broke both halves of the commandment. They passed their seed through the fire, and they profaned His name: “when they had slain their children to their idols, then they came the same day into my sanctuary to profane it”. Blood in their hands, and the same day in His house.

One foot in and one foot out. It is exactly as we still do when we sin all night and sit in church the next morning. They defiled His sanctuary and profaned His sabbaths in the midst of His own house.

precepts.text: Harlots try to entice with the eyes, which is why the Most High wants our sisters to be shame-faced rather than painting the eyes for enticement.
precepts.point: A voice of a multitude at ease was with her, and Sabeans and drunkards were brought from the wilderness who put bracelets on her hands and crowns on her head; being old in adulteries, the nations went in unto her as men go in unto a harlot.

note.label: Ezekiel 23: Aholah and Aholibah, the Two Harlot Sisters

precepts.why:
For the men she sent for from far, she “paintedst thy eyes, and deckedst thyself with ornaments”. “The whoredom of a woman may be known in her haughty looks and eyelids.” Harlots try to entice with the eyes. That is why she painted them.

She washed herself, painted her eyes, decked herself, and sat “upon a stately bed, and a table prepared before it, whereupon thou hast set mine incense and mine oil.” Like an adulteress fixing herself up in her husband's house with his own things to lie with another man, we prepared the bed with the Most High's own incense and oil for the nations. Being old in adulteries, the nations went in unto her “as they go in unto a woman that playeth the harlot”.

This is why the Most High wants our sisters to be shame-faced, not painting the eyes for enticement. Painted eyes and haughty looks are the mark of the whoredom of a woman, and they are the mark of Aholah and Aholibah, the lewd women.
